chunks: And Abu Muhammad al-Muhammadi (may Allah be pleased with him) informed me from Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl ibn Thammam (may Allah have mercy on him) who said: I heard Abu Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Zakkuzaki (may Allah have mercy on him)

and we had mentioned the Book of Taklif, and it was our belief that it was not possessed except by the Ghalis (Exaggerators). This was because, at the beginning when we started writing traditions, we heard him saying: 'What did Ibn Abi Azaqir have in the Book of Taklif?' He would only refine the chapter and bring it to the Shaykh Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh (may Allah be pleased with him), present it to him and scrutinize it. When the chapter was authenticated, it would be sent out, and he would transfer it and order us to make a copy. Meaning that which Husayn ibn Ruh (may Allah be pleased with him) ordered them to do. Abu Ja'far said: 'I wrote it into the Idraj with my own hand in Baghdad.' Ibn Thammam said: 'I said to him: Please, my master, hand it to me so I may write it from your handwriting.' He said to me: 'It has gone out of my hand.' Ibn Thammam said: 'So I went out and took it from someone else and wrote it after I had heard this story.'

key_terms.ابْنُ أَبِي الْعَزَاقِرِ: Ibn Abi Azaqir, a key figure associated with the text
key_terms.الشَّيْخُ أَبُو الْقَاسِمُ الْحُسَيْنُ ب: The Shaykh Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh, the major emissary
key_terms.الْإِدْرَاجُ: Idraj, a method of writing or compiling texts
key_terms.غَالٍ: Ghalis, referring to the 'Exaggerators' in the Imams' status
key_terms.كِتَابُ التَّكْلِيفِ: The Book of Taklif, a specific theological/jurisprudential text

ai.seo_question: Who possessed the Kitab al-Taklif and how was it authenticated by the Imams' emissaries?
ai.summary: This narrative clarifies the transmission history of the *Kitab al-Taklif*, correcting the misconception that it was exclusively held by the *Ghalis* (Exaggerators) by detailing how the eminent emissary Husayn ibn Ruh authenticated and refined the text before its dissemination. The account highlights the rigorous scholarly process in Baghdad, where figures like Abu Ja'far and Ibn Thammam verified the chain of custody and copied the work, thereby establishing its authenticity within Shia hadith literature.
